interpretation: Channel 27 with AMUSE-derived peak (3.07 cm^2/g) contributes delta_log_Z = -0.898 (penalizes the fit) and shifts posterior median sigma/m_0 from 0.59 to 1.77 cm^2/g (+0.48 dex = 3.0x upward). The NEGATIVE delta log Z is HONEST concerning: the AMUSE-derived peak (3.07 cm^2/g at v=358) is in TENSION with the 11-channel model (which prefers sigma/m(v=358) ~ 0.4 cm^2/g via v-dep with a ~ 1.1). This is either (a) simulation-derived peak too high due to N=1024 noise, (b) 11-channel model biased low, or (c) a real model-vs-simulation disagreement that warrants deeper investigation.
honest_caveats: AMUSE simulation is N=1024 per halo, ~100x below publication-grade
SIDM kernel is uniform Gaussian perturbation, not Rutherford-like pairwise scattering
No baryonic physics (gas stripping + star formation post-hoc)
Time slice at t=300 Myr is heuristic; NGC 1052 timescale is ~8 Gyr
Sigmoid fit uses 6 data points; formal uncertainty likely underestimated
Channel 27 width is 1.0 dex (factor-of-10 Gaussian), so peak location matters less than ordering
